subject.title: [Bug]: apply_patch auto-injected into cron job toolsAllow despite explicit exclusion

question: Should cron agentTurn `toolsAllow` be treated as concrete exclusive runtime tool names, or should it keep normal tool-policy semantics where allowing `write` also allows `apply_patch`?
rationale: The source path is clear, but either outcome changes a security boundary or preserves a surprising restriction gap; automation cannot decide the intended operator contract.

options.title: Make cron toolsAllow concrete
options.body: Treat explicit cron `toolsAllow` entries as exact normalized tool ids after group expansion, so `write` no longer implies `apply_patch` for cron payload persistence, with docs and tests updated.

options.title: Keep policy semantics
options.body: Keep `write` granting `apply_patch` everywhere and update cron docs/CLI wording so users know `apply_patch` must be excluded through broader policy rather than an omitted cron allow entry.

options.title: Add a cron deny surface
options.body: Add a separate per-cron deny or restriction surface so users can keep `write` while explicitly denying `apply_patch`, accepting the extra API/config surface.

recommendation.title: Make cron toolsAllow concrete
recommendation.body: Treat explicit cron `toolsAllow` entries as exact normalized tool ids after group expansion, so `write` no longer implies `apply_patch` for cron payload persistence, with docs and tests updated.

likelyOwner.reason: The central code path is the cron persistence-time cap introduced by the scheduled tool policy work.
